findings.text: _sessions_to_sweep drops a session entirely when ANY of its pointers is a known foreign host, while the predicate is host-local and symmetric: a session whose runs were launched on two hosts is skipped by the station on each of them, and a station-attached follower no longer sweeps at all (crew_follow_commands.py:2169 drives subscriber.wake and never _sweep_on_cadence), so that session's resume and review reflex runs nowhere until its pointers drain.

live_work_reading returns False for a reading older than 90 s, and its only caller (crew_follow_commands.py:1633 _is_live) reads False as 'no work', so a station stalled past the stale window settles every attached pane over live work after the grace; the docstring claims a stale reading 'answers nothing rather than a stale verdict', which the caller does not honour, and a station reload long enough to cross the window has the same effect.

_live_work_populations re-states the live-work judgement that crew_follow_commands.py:585 _population_has_live_work already owns (skip a terminal phase, count an ownerless pointer for every session), so one rule now lives in two modules and a change to either the terminal vocabulary or the unowned rule must be made in both.
